title: Walk down Main Street at the original Disneyland
description: The only park Walt Disney personally walked, opened in 1955 on a former orange grove. Two parks now, and the Anaheim original is still the smallest.

title: Do all four parks at Walt Disney World
description: Magic Kingdom, EPCOT, Hollywood Studios and Animal Kingdom across 100 square kilometres - roughly the size of San Francisco, and its own governing district.

title: Ride the Hogwarts Express between Universal's two parks
description: The train only runs if you hold a park-to-park ticket, and the view out the window differs depending on which direction you travel. Epic Universe opened in 2025.

title: Take the studio backlot tram at Universal Studios Hollywood
description: A working studio with a theme park attached rather than the other way round - the tram runs through sets still used for filming.

title: Ride every coaster at Cedar Point
description: Seventeen roller coasters on a sand spit in Lake Erie, and widely regarded by enthusiasts as the best coaster collection anywhere on earth.

title: Survive the coaster count at Six Flags Magic Mountain
description: Twenty roller coasters, more than any park in the world, including one that launches you to 160km/h in under four seconds.

title: Ride the Dollywood coasters through the Smokies
description: Repeatedly voted the best theme park in the world by industry awards, built around Appalachian craft, bluegrass and Dolly Parton's own foundation.

title: Eat the fried chicken at Knott's Berry Farm
description: America's first theme park, which grew out of a roadside berry stand and a chicken dinner restaurant that still has the longest queue on site.

title: Ride through the chocolate factory town at Hersheypark
description: Built in 1906 as a picnic ground for chocolate factory workers. The streetlights in town are shaped like Hershey's Kisses, and the whole place smells of it.

title: Ride the Leviathan at Canada's Wonderland
description: Canada's largest park, with more roller coasters than anywhere outside the US, built around an artificial mountain you can walk inside.

title: Float the underground rivers at Xcaret
description: An eco-archaeological park built over Mayan ruins, where you snorkel through cave rivers and finish with a three-hour show of Mexican regional dance.

title: See the castle at Disneyland Paris
description: Le Chateau de la Belle au Bois Dormant is the most elaborate of all the Disney castles, with a stained-glass gallery upstairs and a dragon in the dungeon below.

title: Ride the wooden coasters at Parc Asterix
description: France's home-grown answer to Disney, built around the comic books, and locally regarded as having far better roller coasters.

title: Work through the countries at Europa-Park
description: Germany's largest park and repeatedly voted the world's best, laid out as eighteen European countries with thirteen coasters between them.

title: Ride Taron at Phantasialand
description: Famously cramped, because the park cannot expand outwards - so it builds upward and through itself, producing some of the most intense theming anywhere.

title: Wander the fairy tale forest at Efteling
description: Older than Disneyland, opened in 1952 around an illustrated fairy tale wood, and still the most atmospheric park in Europe after dark.

title: Ride the wooden coaster at Tivoli Gardens
description: Open since 1843 in the middle of Copenhagen. Walt Disney visited twice and took notes; its 1914 wooden coaster still carries a brakeman on every train.

title: Visit Bakken, the oldest amusement park in the world
description: Operating since 1583, when a spring was discovered here and entertainers followed the crowds. Free to enter, and set in a royal deer park.

title: Ride Helix at Liseberg
description: Scandinavia's largest park, built on a hillside so the coasters run down natural terrain, and transformed into a Christmas market each December.

title: Ride Nemesis at Alton Towers
description: Planning rules capped ride height at the treeline, so the coasters were dug into the ground instead - which is why Nemesis runs through a trench.

title: Ride Shambhala at PortAventura
description: Six themed worlds on the Costa Daurada, with one of Europe's tallest coasters and a Ferrari Land next door.

title: Spend a day at Gardaland
description: Italy's largest park, on the shore of Lake Garda, with a SeaLife aquarium attached and a genuinely good pirate dark ride.

title: Ride Journey to the Center of the Earth at Tokyo DisneySea
description: DisneySea exists nowhere else and is widely held to be the most beautifully themed park ever built - a volcano at its centre that actually erupts.

title: Visit Super Nintendo World at Universal Studios Japan
description: The first Super Nintendo World anywhere, where a wristband lets you collect coins by punching blocks around the land.

title: Ride the coasters under Mount Fuji at Fuji-Q Highland
description: Several record-breaking coasters with Fuji filling the horizon, plus a haunted hospital attraction that takes about an hour to walk through.

title: Ride the Mystic Manor at Hong Kong Disneyland
description: The smallest Disney park, but home to Mystic Manor - a trackless dark ride built here because Chinese custom made a haunted house a poor fit.

title: Take the cable car over the headland at Ocean Park
description: Half marine park, half thrill park, split across a headland and joined by a cable car and a funicular through the rock.

title: See the largest Disney castle at Shanghai Disneyland
description: The Enchanted Storybook Castle is the biggest Disney has built and the only one belonging to no single princess. Opened 2016, and Tron runs here best.

title: Ride the T Express at Everland
description: South Korea's largest park, with one of the steepest wooden coasters in the world and a tulip festival that draws as many people as the rides.

title: Skate the indoor rink at Lotte World
description: The largest indoor theme park on earth, with an outdoor island section on a lake, connected by monorail and open whatever the weather does.

title: Spend a day at Universal Studios Singapore
description: Compact enough to do properly in one day, on a resort island reached by cable car, monorail or a boardwalk you can simply walk across.

title: Ride Formula Rossa at Ferrari World
description: The fastest roller coaster in the world at 240km/h, which is quick enough that riders are issued safety goggles before boarding.

title: Ride the Wild Mouse at Luna Park Sydney
description: Under the Harbour Bridge since 1935, behind a giant grinning face. The 1959 Wild Mouse is one of the last of its kind still running anywhere.
